title: Are Neural Networks Already Clean?
standfirst: Goodfire's claim that most neurons have one main job set off one of the year's fiercest AI debates. What the released evidence supports, and the question it cannot yet answer.
summary: Goodfire's October 2026 essay estimates that about 90% of Qwen3-32B neuron poles have one main job. A sourced account of the claim, the reaction and an Evidence Press audit of the released gallery: the labels are coherent by Goodfire's AI-reviewed rubric, but the gallery is not a whole-model sample and the developmental explanation is untested.

banner.alt: Left, a chain from the letters iy to diy to the phrase do it yourself. Right, two possible histories, related branching and packing of unrelated uses, both point to that same endpoint.
banner.caption: Schematic of the essay's own example and the two rival explanations it contrasts. It shows no measured data.

claimBoundary: A sourced commentary on claims and reactions reported as of 20 October 2026, including the results of an Evidence Press secondary audit of public data: a fixed random sample of 100 reports from Goodfire's published gallery, a mechanical recount of their published review labels, reanalysis of 6,901 exported intervention rows, layer counts of the full gallery, and an offline analysis of one external replication's published report. No model was run, no neuron was re-judged and Goodfire's experiments were not replicated. The audit's numbers were replayed offline from retained extracts; that checks extraction and arithmetic, not the truth of any semantic label. The proposed confirmatory study has not been run. Nothing here is peer reviewed or independently reproduced.
